page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is provided by a single bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 22 GB of dedicated VRAM. This server configuration does not include local NVMe storage.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance divergence between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The CPU exhibits weak single-core and multi-core performance in Geekbench and stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks register in the lower tier. Conversely, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in the top 10% for large language model inference. Specifically, prompt processing for a medium 7B model reaches 2225.82 tokens per second, while text generation for the same model achieves 52.31 tokens per second. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the g2-standard-8 offers a specialized hardware profile where cost efficiency is realized through GPU-offloaded tasks rather than raw CPU compute. The weak CPU performance makes it inefficient for heavy general-purpose compilation or CPU-only processing. However, the high-efficiency LLM inference capabilities make it highly suitable for small to medium machine learning model deployment, AI inference pipelines, and graphics-accelerated workloads that do not require local storage.
